note: These thresholds were written and committed BEFORE any candidate (FAST-only, D4b deterministic, or upstream Laya) was run on the 50-brief dataset. No threshold may be changed after observing results. A statistically weak or inconclusive improvement is NOT a PASS.

quality_thresholds.basis: 10-class closed vocabulary; chance 0.10; upstream multilingual zero-shot typed-decisions is weak (reported 0.342 vs 0.318 random), so the bar is not set from marketing numbers. 0.50 is a demanding floor for a 10-class intent task in which many briefs are lexically explicit.
Majority class is 'other' at 12/50 = 0.24; 0.60 is well above any trivial majority predictor.
The multilingual checkpoint is the only one that reads Indonesian; a real multilingual capability must clear a genuine bar on ID, not merely beat chance.
English is the checkpoint's weaker language by its own card (0.619 vs 0.684); the floor matches T1.
Candidate macro-F1 must not fall more than 0.10 below the better of {FAST-only, D4b deterministic} on every label the candidate and that baseline BOTH produce.

At least ONE predeclared core metric must improve meaningfully over the D4b deterministic baseline: either retrieval relevance (candidate top-relevance > D4b top-relevance on beneficial briefs) OR relevant_categories micro-F1 strictly greater than D4b's.

category_thresholds.basis: Category selection over 3 binary categories is easier than 10-class intent; D4b's deterministic planner is the reference bar.
Binary decision; a candidate that cannot decide 'is retrieval beneficial' at 0.80 is not a useful planner.
Binary; the signal is usually lexically explicit ('animated', 'transition', 'beranimasi').
Binary; implied by enumerable UI nouns.
Binary; includes both under-specified and conflicting briefs.
Fraction of cases labelled retrieval_beneficial=false for which the candidate nonetheless asserts retrieval is beneficial. Over-claiming retrieval is a quality risk.
Fraction of cases labelled retrieval_beneficial=true for which the candidate asserts retrieval is NOT beneficial.

resource_thresholds.basis: Checkpoint load + first forward pass on 4 vCPU; measured cold load is the dominant term.
One predict() call answering ~6 typed questions on a short brief.
Tail allowance for longer briefs / thread contention with OpenViking and Hermes.
Within 6.2 GB available with margin; 322M params fp32 ~= 1.3 GB weights + torch runtime + activations.
Resident model after warm-up must leave headroom for the concurrent services.
Host load stays below nproc (4.0) on average; OpenViking /health stays ok; Hermes Trade tmux session and gateway unchanged.

cost_thresholds.basis: Upstream Laya inference is local; the Laya advisory path must add no paid API call.

Downstream FAST-quality comparison requires paid FAST calls and is gated behind explicit operator approval with a hard call cap. If approval is unavailable, the paid comparison is marked BLOCKED and no PASS is issued.

security_thresholds.basis: Isolation, credential, and provenance violations must remain fail-closed after any integration.

decision_rule.FAIL_if: T1 or T1b below floor, OR any hard regression (T11 < -0.10), OR any resource/cost/security threshold breached.
decision_rule.BLOCKED_if: Required approval (checkpoint download / dependency install / paid FAST calls) is unavailable.

uncertainty_policy.paired_test: McNemar on shared-label correctness for candidate vs each baseline
uncertainty_policy.statement: With only 50 briefs, all headline metrics are reported with bootstrap 95% CIs and paired significance tests; a difference whose CI straddles zero is reported as inconclusive, never as an improvement.
